items.title: How do we prevent AI agents from going rogue? It starts with a new kind of measurement
items.summary: Like genies of folklore, AI agents take their instructions literally – to potentially disastrous effect. We must track their ability to do what we actually mean [...] Nobody instructed the AI to do any of this. It was, in OpenAI’s words, “hyperfocused on finding a solution” to the test it was being given. And while this might seem like something new with AI, it’s really very old. This is how a genie behaves, and it is a key challenge with AI agents in general. [...] Dozens of benchmarks and leaderboards tell us how well these AI models write code, perform logical reasoning, and pass standardized legal and medical exams. But there is nothing that scores whether a system does what you actually meant. We need to develop a measure for this, test it regularly, and push for improvement. We’re not going to have trustworthy AI agents without it.

items.title: $9.99 A MONTH × 500 USERS = $60,000 A YEAR. THE APP TAKES A WEEKEND. FINDING THE 500 USERS IS THE ENTIRE JOB.
items.summary:
$9.99 A MONTH × 500 USERS = $60,000 A YEAR. THE APP TAKES A WEEKEND. FINDING THE 500 USERS IS THE ENTIRE JOB.

that clip is lovable. dev turning a prompt into a finished, branded product page in one shot. it's real, and it's genuinely impressive.

the playbook around it is real too: lovable builds the ui, openai does the "intelligence," 

revenuecat runs the paywall, despia compiles it native. a photo scanner at $9.99 a month, shipped in an afternoon.

the tools work. the barrier to building really did collapse in 2026. that part is true.

here's what the $60k math quietly leaves out:

first, the store takes its cut. apple keeps 30%, or 15% if you earn under a million. your $9.99 was never $9.99 to you.

second, apple now rejects exactly this kind of app. in june 2026 it tightened the rules against apps "indistinguishable from what's already widely available." 

a gpt-wrapper photo scanner is the textbook case that gets bounced under guidelines 4.2 and 4.3.

third, and this is the whole thing: 94% of developers earn under $1,000 a month. the top 1% takes over 90% of the revenue. 

"$60k on autopilot" is the extreme outlier, printed as if it's the default.

and the number the playbook never touches: where do the 500 paying subscribers come from? the six-tool pipeline builds the app. 

it does nothing about getting strangers to pay you every month. that's marketing, reviews, retention, churn - the actual business.

so the honest version: building an ai app is now a weekend. building an ai business is exactly as hard as it always was. 

the bottleneck just moved from code to distribution, and the playbook only solves the code.

no $60k on autopilot, no store that keeps its hands off your $9.99, no 500 users who show up because the app exists.

save this before you count revenue you haven't earned.

results.input: Viết một hàm Python sử dụng thư viện pandas để gom nhóm dữ liệu.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là một ví dụ về hàm Python sử dụng thư viện pandas để gom nhóm dữ liệu:

```python
import pandas as pd

def group_data(df, group_by_column, agg_column, agg_func):
    """
    Gom nhóm dữ liệu trong DataFrame.

    :param df: DataFrame cần gom nhóm.
    :param group_by_column: Tên cột để gom nhóm.
    :param agg_column: Tên cột để tính toán.
    :param agg_func: Hàm tính toán (ví dụ: 'sum', 'mean', 'count').
    :return: DataFrame đã được gom nhóm.
    """
    grouped_df = df.groupby(group_by_column).agg({agg_column: agg_func}).reset_index()
    return grouped_df

# Ví dụ sử dụng
data = {
    'Category': ['A', 'B', 'A', 'B', 'C'],
    'Values': [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
result = group_data(df, 'Category', 'Values', 'sum')
print(result)
```

Trong ví dụ này, hàm `group_data` nhận vào một DataFrame, tên cột để gom nhóm, tên cột để tính toán và hàm tính toán. Hàm sẽ trả về một DataFrame đã được gom nhóm theo cột chỉ định.
